candidate.answerReason: The conjugate factors have product 1, giving \(x+\sqrt{x^2-1}=10\) and \(x-\sqrt{x^2-1}=1/10\). Hence \(x=101/20\), and the requested expression simplifies to \(2x^2=51.005\).

methods.label: Use reciprocal pairs
methods.explanation:
The radicals occur in pairs whose product simplifies by the difference-of-squares identity. This lets us replace reciprocals without expanding complicated radicals.

For the original expression to be real, \(x^2\ge1\). Put \(s=\sqrt{x^2-1}\), so \(s\ge0\). Then
\[
(x+s)(x-s)=x^2-s^2=1.
\]
Neither factor is zero, and \(1/(x-s)=x+s\). The given equation therefore becomes
\[
2(x+s)=20,
\]
so \(x+s=10\). Its reciprocal partner is \(x-s=1/10\). Adding these two equations gives
\[
2x=10+\frac1{10},
\qquad x=\frac{101}{20}.
\]
This value is admissible: \(s=99/20\), so \(x+s=10\) and \(x-s=1/10\), which satisfy the original equation.

For the requested expression, put \(t=\sqrt{x^4-1}\). It is real because \(x^2\ge1\), and
\[
(x^2+t)(x^2-t)=1.
\]
Also \(x^2+t\ge1\), so its reciprocal is defined and equals \(x^2-t\). Thus the radical terms cancel:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^2+t+\frac1{x^2+t}
&=(x^2+t)+(x^2-t)\\
&=2x^2\\
&=2\left(\frac{101}{20}\right)^2\\
&=\frac{10201}{200}=51.005.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{51.005}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
